h1: The 5 Best Office Chairs With Headrests of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Headrest Office Chairs 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five high-back office chairs with headrests or fixed head support, compared on lumbar design, mesh versus leather and price.
summary: The Marsail mesh chair is the best overall pick: a named headrest, adjustable lumbar and 3D arms on a back that breathes. The GTPLAYER Big and Tall is the one to buy if you need a 400 lb rating. Under $100, the white GTPLAYER confirms a headrest and footrest. The Furmax looks the part but never confirms head support.
intro: Here is the trap in this category: a tall back is not a headrest. Listings love the phrase "high back" because it photographs well, and then the buyer leans back during a long call and finds nothing behind the skull. Executive chairs are the worst offenders, since the padding stops at the shoulders.

So this ranking starts from the head and works down. We reviewed five chairs that either name a headrest outright or use a fixed tall back as head support, then scored them on the Primea framework. Headrest status carried the most weight, followed by lumbar design, adjustability, upholstery and price tier. Mid-back chairs and one executive model with no stated head support did not make the list.

products.name: Marsail Ergonomic Office Chair, Office Desk Chair with High Back Mesh and Adjustable Lumbar Support, Rolling Work Swivel Task Chairs with Wheel 3D Armrests and Headrest
products.verdict: A confirmed headrest on a breathable mesh back with adjustable arms.
products.description:
The Marsail pairs the one feature this guide exists for, a confirmed headrest, with a high-back mesh frame, adjustable lumbar support and 3D adjustable armrests. Mesh matters more than it sounds: it lets heat escape through the back, where foam and leather hold it against you through an eight hour day.

It wins because every adjustment a desk worker actually uses is present and none of them is a gimmick. The GTPLAYER Big and Tall adds a footrest and a 400 lb rating, but its saddle cushion and upholstery run warmer, and its gaming shape looks out of place in an office.

Buy it if you sit upright for hours in a warm room. The caveat is the missing footrest, so you will not get a lie-back-and-rest posture, and the $100 to $200 tier costs more than the chairs below.
products.idealFor: Long desk days in warm rooms.

products.name: GTPLAYER Big and Tall Gaming Chair 400lbs Heavy Duty Office Chair with Foot Rest and Ergonomic Pocket Spring Lumbar Support, High Back 3D Saddle Shaped Cushion for Back Pain Relief, Matte-Black
products.verdict: A 400 lb rating, pocket spring lumbar and a footrest.
products.description:
The GTPLAYER Big and Tall is the only chair here that publishes a weight rating, 400 lb, and that number is the reason it takes second place. It adds a pocket spring lumbar system, a 3D saddle shaped cushion, a headrest and a footrest, all in the $100 to $200 tier.

Pocket springs flex with your posture, which a fixed foam pad cannot do. Against the Marsail, though, the gaming upholstery traps more heat and the shape reads as a streamer's chair rather than a desk chair, so it drops one place despite carrying more load.

Buy it if you are a larger user or recline often and want your feet up. Skip it if the room runs hot or the chair sits in a client-facing office, because the styling and surface material both work against you there.
products.skipIf: You want a quiet office look.

products.name: GTPLAYER Gaming Chair, Computer Chair with Footrest and Lumbar Support, Height Adjustable Game Chair with 360 Degree Swivel Seat and Headrest and for Office or Gaming, Pearl White
products.verdict: A confirmed headrest and footrest for under $100.
products.description:
The white GTPLAYER is the cheapest way to get a headrest that the listing actually confirms. For the $50 to $100 tier you also get a footrest, lumbar support, a 360 degree swivel and height adjustment, which covers the basics of a head-supporting chair.

It sits below the Big and Tall model for a plain reason: no weight rating is stated. A chair without a published capacity leaves heavier users guessing about the gas lift and base, and it has no pocket spring lumbar either. It beats the N-GEN below because the headrest is confirmed rather than implied by a tall back.

Buy it for a student desk or a gaming corner. Skip it if you are over 250 lb, since nothing in the listing backs that load.
products.idealFor: Students and gamers on a budget.

products.name: N-GEN GAMING Video Gaming Chair with Footrest Lumbar Support for Home Office High Back Recliner Height Adjustable Ergonomic Comfy Leather Computer Desk Chair, Carbon Black
products.verdict: A fixed tall back doubles as head support and leans back.
products.description:
The N-GEN is a recliner first and a task chair second. Its fixed high back is meant to double as head support, and it adds leather upholstery, a footrest and height adjustment in the $50 to $100 tier.

A fixed back is the weakness. It supports your head only if your torso length matches the chair's, and nothing on it moves to meet a taller or shorter sitter. That is why it ranks under the white GTPLAYER, which confirms a headrest, even though both cost the same.

Buy it if you recline often and want the footrest, and your height sits near the middle of the range. Skip it if you want an adjustable neck pillow. Leather also runs warm, so expect sticking in a summer room without air conditioning.
products.skipIf: You want an adjustable neck pillow.

products.name: Furmax Office Executive Chair, High Back Adjustable Managerial Home Desk Chair, Swivel PU Leather Chair with Lumbar Support
products.verdict: Executive looks, but head support is not confirmed.
products.description:
The Furmax is the best looking chair in this ranking and the weakest answer to the question asked. It has a tall PU leather back, lumbar support, adjustable height and a managerial profile, all in the $50 to $100 tier.

Its position comes down to one omission: the listing never says a headrest is included. Head support here rests on the height of the back alone, which fails for anyone who leans past the top edge. Every other chair above it either names a headrest or builds one into a recliner shape.

Buy it for a formal office where appearance counts and you rarely lean back. If neck support is the goal, add a clip-on pillow after checking the back is wide and sturdy enough, or choose any of the four picks above.
products.idealFor: Formal offices that want a managerial look.

whatMatters.detail: A true headrest is a separate cushion that catches your skull when you lean back, while a tall back only works if it happens to match your height. The difference decides whether your neck muscles stay loaded during calls. On a listing, search the bullets for the word "headrest" itself. "High back" alone proves nothing, as the Furmax shows.

Lumbar support fills the curve of your lower spine so your pelvis stops rolling backward as you tire. Pocket spring designs, like the one in the GTPLAYER Big and Tall, flex as you shift, while foam pads stay put. Check whether the support moves up and down, because a fixed pad lands in the wrong place on many torsos.

Upholstery sets how the chair feels at hour six. Mesh, as on the Marsail, lets heat out. PU leather and leather wipe clean but hold warmth against your back, which is why the Furmax and N-GEN run hotter. Pick by room temperature first and cleaning habits second. The material is named in the title or the spec list.

The weight rating is the maximum load the base, casters and gas lift are certified to carry. A chair near its limit wears faster and can feel unstable when you recline. Only the GTPLAYER Big and Tall states one here, at 400 lb. If a listing omits the number, as the white GTPLAYER does, ask the seller before ordering.

Armrests that move up, down and sideways let you slide the chair under a desk and keep your shoulders relaxed. Fixed arms often block the chair from tucking in and force your elbows into the wrong position. The Marsail lists 3D armrests, the term to look for. Flip-up arms are a useful variant if your desk is low.

faq.q: Do I need a headrest on an office chair?
faq.a: Not for upright typing, but yes if you lean back during calls or reading. A headrest like the Marsail's takes load off the neck muscles when you recline, which is where most tension builds in long sessions.
Assuming a high back includes a headrest. The Furmax has a tall back but the listing never confirms head support. Search the bullets for the word "headrest" and treat its absence as a no.

faq.q: Is a gaming chair worth it over an office chair?
faq.a: For reclining and a footrest, yes: the GTPLAYER Big and Tall and N-GEN both include one. For hot rooms or formal offices, the Marsail's mesh back is the better chair, because gaming upholstery holds heat.

faq.q: How hard are these to assemble?
faq.a: Allow under an hour to attach the base, casters, gas lift and seat on chairs like the Marsail or GTPLAYER. A second person helps when you bolt on the back, since the assembled weight is awkward to line up alone.

faq.q: How do I clean leather upholstery?
faq.a: Wipe with a damp cloth and mild soap, the routine for the Furmax and N-GEN. Skip harsh cleaners and solvents, which can crack PU surfaces over time. Mesh, like the Marsail's, needs only a vacuum brush pass.

faq.q: Can I add a headrest to a chair without one?
faq.a: Yes, clip-on headrests exist, and they are the usual fix for the Furmax. Fit varies, so confirm the back is wide and sturdy enough to hold the clamp before buying, or choose a chair that includes one.

finalTake: For most desks, the Marsail is the chair to buy: a named headrest, adjustable lumbar and a mesh back that stays cool. Larger users who recline should step up to the GTPLAYER Big and Tall for its 400 lb rating. Under $100, the white GTPLAYER confirms a headrest and adds a footrest. Treat the Furmax as a style purchase and verify head support before you order anything else.
